recaps.title: A shootout, a goalie with an assist, and a four-goal lead that went missing
text: Arnie Jordan here, coming to you from row three at Jordan Arena, with the Rinkside Report. I had company in row three this week. A fella in a toque sat down beside me with a cowbell, and every time somebody scored, he rang it. Thirty-five goals. By the third game I was ready to buy that cowbell off him just to bury it. And a lady one row down asked me if I was the podcast guy. I said yes. She said, oh, I thought you'd be taller. I was sitting down. It was Sunday, October twenty-fifth.

First, a word for the stripes. Shane and Chip had the whistles, three games back to back, and I'd bet they skated more miles than any team out there. They called eight penalties all night, and they found a way to call three of them on the same man. More on him in a minute.

The early game was the Regatta Nordiques against Dawson's Oilers. Whetlam opened the scoring, from Langlois and Roy, and Craigy tied it late in the first, set up by McPherson and, I checked this twice, Dawson. The goalie. A goalie with an assist. That man passes better than half the fellas skating in front of him.

Now, I started a new page in the notebook, and at the top I wrote one word: Stuart. Two trips in the first period and a hook in the second. Nine minutes in the box. Shane and Chip were waving him over there like a parking attendant. And Craigy's tying goal came while Stuart was sitting in there. Shorthanded. Craigy, cleaning up after his teammate like a fella with a mop at a wedding. The Nordiques kept Stuart company: Andersen and Pulo for tripping, and Whetlam for a high stick, so Whetlam had a goal and a penalty. The full combo meal.

McPherson put the Oilers ahead in the second, and Trigg came in to replace McKay in the Nordiques net. In the third, Pulo tied it and Lawrence put the Nordiques ahead, then McPherson tied it again with forty seconds to go. Overtime solved nothing, so off to a shootout, and Moorzy buried it. Four to three Nordiques. McPherson had two goals and an assist and went home with nothing. That's baking the whole cake and getting handed a cracker.

Game two, the Culp Habs beat the Keg Canucks eight to three. Penney had the hat trick and an assist, Hering and Dixon each had a goal and three helpers, Clark had three assists, and Paul scored twice. Koke, McMillan and Adam Short scored for the Canucks. Halfway through, both teams changed goalies at the exact same second, again. Rennie and Rico out, The Plug and Levar in. Two weeks running. Next week I expect a dance number. And not one penalty all game. Shane and Chip either had the quietest hour of their lives, or they left their whistles in the car.

Now, I have to tell you about upstairs. Behind the glass, up top, that's where you'll find the fellas who already played. Hot dogs in one hand, pizza in the other, telling the story of the goal they scored an hour ago, and it gets prettier every time. And every time their team scores down below, they pound on that glass like it owes them money, and they holler, and they cheer. And then one of them always turns around and asks, can they hear us down there? Fellas, I'm in row three, and I can hear you. I can hear you chewing.

Then the late game, the ColdBreak Leafs against the Timbit Senators, and friends, sit down. The Senators led seven to three in the second. Obie had two goals and two assists, Simon Murphy had two goals, and Deakin, Holt and Sheridan chipped in. Holt and Sheridan scored fifty-four seconds apart while Adams sat for tripping. I took out a pen, a pen, and wrote: Senators in a cakewalk.

The Leafs then scored seven in a row. Parsons got one late in the second, and Haroutunian scored forty-seven seconds into the third. Then Collini scored three goals in one minute and fifty-five seconds. A hat trick in less time than it takes me to climb to row three. The cowbell nearly caught fire. Parsons scored again, and Darren Horton finished it all by himself with fifty-one seconds left. Ten to seven Leafs. Horton had five points, Parsons and Pierce had four each. Upstairs, the glass took a beating. And Senators, Halloween's next weekend. You got your fright in early.

So that's your week: a shootout, a goalie with an assist, a man with his own page in my notebook, and a four-goal lead that went missing. Thanks to Shane and Chip for keeping the peace, and for keeping Stuart busy. If I got your name wrong, or gave your goal to the fella beside you, take it up with the refs, the timekeeper, and how fast you people move out there. Tape your sticks. This has been Arnie Jordan with the Rinkside Report.

recaps.title: Two six-to-five finishes, two hat tricks and a goalie swap that looked like a fire drill
text: Arnie Jordan here, coming to you from row three at Jordan Arena, with the Rinkside Report. Welcome back to both of my listeners. It was Sunday, October eighteenth, and after a week off I showed up with a fresh notebook, two sharpened pencils and a large coffee. I left with half a notebook, one pencil, and a napkin covered in arrows. Thirty goals, three games, and two of them won by a single goal.

The early game was the Regatta Nordiques against the Culp Habs, and Fissel scored forty-five seconds in, set up by Regular. Hunt tied it for the Habs, then Regular scored one himself late in the first, and another in the second, from Brophy and DeBolster. With a name like Regular, you'd expect a regular night. Two goals and an assist? I'd call it premium.

The rest of that second period was a parade to the penalty box. Brophy went for hooking, Paul went for tripping, and DeBolster went for something the timekeeper wrote down so fast I couldn't read it from row three. Two Nordiques in the box in one period, and the Habs didn't score on either one. Somewhere in there a clearing attempt went so high I lost it in the lights. I believe it came down during the second game. I did not see who shot it, and I have decided not to find out.

Paul made up for his trip early in the third, making it three to two, but Moorzy and Fissel answered a minute and a half apart, with Roy setting up both. Hunt got his second, and that's how it ended, five to three Nordiques. Paul had a goal, two assists and a trip to the box, which in this league is what we call a full evening. Trigg went the distance and held the Habs to three.

Game two was the Timbit Senators against the Keg Canucks, and I started a tally of lead changes on my napkin. Davies scored late in the first, and Buynink stopped everything in that period, then handed the net to Shannon. One perfect period, and the rest of the night off.

Then came the second period, and I am still recovering. Seven goals. Williams went to the box for hooking ten seconds in. Ten seconds. I was still blowing on my coffee. Obie made it two nothing, and then the Canucks scored three in a little over three minutes: Pundy, Adam Short, and Leyenhorst. The Senators came back with Sheridan and Davies again, and Leyenhorst got his second to tie it at four. Around goal number six, my first pencil snapped clean in half.

Martin put the Canucks ahead to start the third, with a goal and three assists on the night. That's two leads for the Canucks, and they gave both of them back, which is very generous. Obie tied it, and Schmidt scored the winner all by himself, no assists, didn't ask anybody. Six to five Senators. And then, with forty-seven seconds left and his team down by one, Pundy went to the box for interference. Best seat in the house for the finish, I'll give him that. Better than row three. Murphy had three helpers, and Shannon gave up five and still got the win.

The late game was Dawson's Oilers and the ColdBreak Leafs, and it turned into a hat trick contest. Foran scored fifty-seven seconds in, then Horton and Grossi traded goals all first period. NoPants and Grossi made it four to two Oilers in the second, before Adams and Pierce tied it right back up. Then, halfway through the period, both teams changed goalies at the same moment. Raimondo and Mallet out, Dawson and Rosie in. I thought it was a fire drill. Rosie had been in net for exactly one minute when Grossi scored his third. Welcome to the game.

In the third, Misek went to the box for tripping, and forty-five seconds later Horton finished his own hat trick to tie it at five. Then McPherson scored the winner, unassisted, with five thirty-six left. Last week he had six points. This week he had one, and it was the one that counted. Grossi finished with five points. Horton and Pierce had four each, and the Leafs got nothing for it but a sore neck from watching the scoreboard.

So that's your week: thirty goals, two hat tricks, two six to five finishes, and a napkin with four lead changes on it, every one of them from game two. If I got your name wrong, or gave your goal to the fella beside you, take it up with the refs, the timekeeper, and how fast you people move out there. Tape your sticks, and wave if you see me in row three. This has been Arnie Jordan with the Rinkside Report.

recaps.title: Thirty-six goals, two six-point nights and one clean game
text: Arnie Jordan here, coming to you from row three at Jordan Arena, with the Rinkside Report, the only hockey podcast with two loyal listeners. Three, if my neighbour remembers. It was Sunday, October fourth. I had a coffee in one hand and a pencil in the other, and I needed both, because we had three games and thirty-six goals. Thirty-six. I ran out of page.

Game one was the Keg Canucks against Dawson's Oilers, and the Oilers put ten on the board in a ten to five win. From where I sat, Ron McPherson was everywhere, with two goals and four assists for six points. That's not a stat line, that's a phone number. Darren Craig had a goal and four helpers, and Mike Foran scored a pair. I will say there was one pass in that game that missed everybody on the ice, and I believe it is still on its way to Vineland. I didn't catch who threw it, and I'm not asking.

But give the Canucks their due. Down seven to two, they could have packed it in. Instead, Daryl Strong and Wes Short scored forty-five seconds apart to close out the second period, both set up by Waylon Tweedy and Kurt Peters, and Paul Koke had two of his own. I barely had the first one written down before the second one went in. The Oilers also took three trips to the penalty box and still won by five, so I'll keep my opinions to myself, at least this week.

Game two. I had just sat back down with a fresh coffee. The ColdBreak Leafs came out flying, with goals from Kevin Pierce, Larry Penney and Adam Steele, and they led three to one after the first period. I wrote the word upset in my notebook. I have since crossed it out, because the Regatta Nordiques scored eight in a row. Josh Moore had the hat trick and three assists, so that's six points for him as well. Doug Lawrence scored twelve seconds into the third, Moore scored again less than a minute later, and that was the hockey game.

Nine to three for the Nordiques, with two goals each for Lawrence and Nick Langlois, and four points for Adam Regular. And a tip of the cap to Kevin Rolston, who came into the Nordiques net halfway through and did not let in a single goal. He made it look so easy that I started wondering if I could do it. I could not. I get winded on the stairs up to row three.

Game three was the late one, the Culp Habs against the Timbit Senators, and the first period was a track meet. Drew Hering scored forty seconds in, before I had even sharpened my pencil, and then he got another. Matt Dixon added a third, and Kevin Paul set up all three of them. But every time the Habs scored, the Senators answered, with Blaine Davies, then Tyler Williams, then Davies again. It was tied at three after one.

After that, the Senators shut the door. Simon Murphy scored with fifty seconds left in the second and again in the third, and Rob Holt added one for insurance, for a six to three final. Davies and Murphy each had two goals and two assists, Dave Sheridan had three helpers, and Tim Shannon came in cold and stopped everything he saw. Somewhere in there, a shot went so wide that it rattled the glass right in front of me. I spilled half my coffee, and I would like the league to know that I am keeping the receipt.

And listen to this. There was not one penalty in that game. Sixty minutes of oldtimers hockey, and nobody went to the box. I keep a whole column in my notebook for penalties, and it is still empty. I didn't think it could be done.

So that's your week: thirty-six goals, two six point nights, and one game as clean as a whistle. If I got your name wrong, or gave your goal to the fella beside you, take it up with the refs, the timekeeper, and how fast you people move out there. All the details are on the league website. Tape your sticks, and give me a wave if you see me in row three on Sunday. This has been Arnie Jordan with the Rinkside Report.
